messages.subject: caching issues
parts:
hi *

hosting a shiny server where i've built a buch of reports and dashboards. in addition to the usual server.r & ui.r files the dashboard consists of a R script tha collects data from half a dozen sources, transforms it and builds plots with ggplot. This processing file is run by cran every 15 minutes and saves the processed data and plots as objects on disc. the server.r picks up the RD objects from the disc

for some reason i seem to get some sort of issues with a cache somewhere. as sometimes the dashboard will not update. if i edit the server.R file save the changes, it does update. Noticed similar behaviour with some Rmarkdown reports i am running. a configuration somewhere i've missed perhaps?

thank you,
Sami Kallinen

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: caching issues
parts:
While your shiny server function is run every time a new browser connects, the server.R file itself is only evaluated 1) when that particular R process first starts up, and 2) when server.R is modified and then a new browser connects. There are a couple of ways you can get the behavior you want.

Option 1: The cron job that does the work can do "touch restart.txt" in the Shiny app directory when it's done. This will force Shiny Server to start a new R process and retire the old one when the next browser arrives.

Option 2: Keep the cron job the way it is, but use reactiveFileReader to create auto-updating versions. This would mean even browsers that are already showing the old data, would automatically update themselves when new data arrives, without needing to reload. You can put the reactiveFileReaders above the shiny server function if the same data is to be shared by everyone.
